subject: Post-call: provider contrast validation & next tests
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Sasha Miranda <sasha.miranda@sagepoint.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Apr 2028 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: provider contrast validation & next tests

Thanks again for the great conversation this morning, Sasha — appreciate the clarity on SagePoint's integration priorities. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're all aligned: 

Summary of what we heard
- Primary goal: reliable, low-cost inference for multi-turn document summarization pipeline with 40k token context windows and 99th-percentile latency targets under 200ms for short lookups.
- Current provider comparison baseline: you're testing hyperscaler-managed endpoints (multi-tenant) plus a small self-hosted baseline. Key gaps you flagged were long-context hallucinations and cost unpredictability.

High-level Redwood differentiators (from the call)
- Prefix / KV cache that preserves multi-turn state without re-tokenizing full context (reduces token cost substantially for repeated docs)
- Intelligent batching and per-route SLOs to control 99th-pct latency for interactive paths
- Transparent performance profiles across model variants and quantization settings (we surface token-level cost deltas)
- Automated fallback routing to compatible model variants to avoid outages when capacity is constrained

Suggested validation matrix (attached: provider_contrast_probe_matrix.xlsx) — proposed priority probes
1) Long-context hallucination probe: 20k / 40k / 60k sequences using your doc corpus, measure hallucination rate (precision of entity preservation) and token amplification (how many extra tokens needed to ground answers).
2) Multi-turn retention: apply 10-turn dialogue with KV caching on/off to quantify context drift and per-turn latency/cost.
3) Reranking throughput/latency: 50 candidates, compare per-call token cost and 95/99 latency percentiles under concurrent load.
4) Quantization variants: int8/q4/q5 variants of the chosen model to profile quality vs CPU/GPU inference delta.
5) Regression sweep: run your canonical prompt suite (suggested set attached eval_prompts_v2.csv) and capture hallucination triggers and top-1 accuracy on labeled QA subsets.

Immediate asks from SagePoint
- Please share the sample corpus (anonymized) and 2–3 canonical prompts for the regression sweep.
- Confirm whether we have permission to run throughput tests against your real traffic patterns or if we should replay a sanitized trace.

Proposed owners & dates
- Redwood: run baseline probe matrix (long-context + reranking) and share first results by 2028-05-07 — Ben (bench), Karthik (model config).
- SagePoint: provide sample corpus + prompts by 2028-05-03 — Sasha / Marco.
- Joint: quick sync 2028-05-09 to review deltas and decide whether Dedicated trial is warranted.

Attachments: provider_contrast_probe_matrix.xlsx (probe matrix), eval_prompts_v2.csv (prompt seed list).

If that all looks right, I'll kick off the runs as soon as we have the sample corpus. Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rachel_kim@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0143

Thanks Rachel — this is exactly the right level of detail. A few clarifications from our side and one ask: 

On the probes
- Long-context hallucination probe: yes, please emphasize entity fidelity checks (we have legal names and PII-stripped IDs we want unchanged across summaries).
- Reranking throughput: we care about tail latency when running 50 candidates concurrently; please capture p95/p99 and CPU/GPU utilization.

What we can provide
- We'll upload an anonymized corpus (5k docs, mixed length) and a sanitized traffic trace to your shared Drive folder by 2028-05-02. Upload will be SagePoint_sample_texts_v1.zip.
- We'll also include 3 canonical prompts and a set of labeled QA pairs for the regression sweep.

Ask from us
- Can Redwood run quantized model variants (q4_0, q5_1 if available) and include a small human-eval batch to check semantic parity?

One more item: we have a pre-sales security checklist that asks about data residency and audit logs; I'll attach the security doc when I upload the corpus.

On cadence: 2028-05-07 baseline results sound good. After that we may ask for a 2-week Dedicated trial if the deltas are promising.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Sasha Miranda
Director of ML Infrastructure | SagePoint Systems
Sasha.Miranda@sagepoint.com

Perfect — thanks Sasha. We'll proceed as outlined. Quick notes on scope and what we'll share with you by 2028-05-07: 

Planned Redwood deliverables (first pass)
- Baseline probe results: long-context hallucination metrics (precision/recall for entity preservation), token amplification, and p95/p99 latency numbers for reranking under 30/60/100 concurrent users.
- Quantized variant comparison: relative quality score on your labeled QA pairs (human-eval + automated metrics) for q4/q5 vs fp16.
- Regression checklist: list of prompts that regressed vs reference outputs and where hallucination spikes occur.

Notes and constraints
- For multi-turn KV caching experiments we'll simulate session stickiness to reproduce your expected traffic; real traffic replay is ideal but sanitized replay works.
- We'll avoid any production writes or data storage beyond ephemeral test benches; results and logs will be persisted only in the shared Drive folder for the project.

Scheduling sync
- I'll schedule a 30-min review for 2028-05-09 11:00 AM PT (calendar invite to follow).

Deliverables attached: eval_prompts_v2.csv (seed prompts + labeling instructions), provider_contrast_probe_matrix.xlsx (detailed matrix + measurement columns).

If anything changes on your side (e.g., you need a narrower quantization list), flag it in the Drive folder and we'll adjust.

Thanks team — Ben / Karthik, please confirm you have capacity to start the probe runs once Sasha uploads the zip.

Best,
Rachel

Forwarding my quick internal checklist now that Sasha confirmed the upload window. High-level items for Redwood ops / bench team: 

1) Bench infra allocation (owner: Ben)
- Reserve one 4xA100 bench cluster and one 8xA10s cluster for parallel runs next week (2028-05-06 -> 2028-05-08). Track utilization and idle time.

2) Model configs (owner: Karthik)
- Prepare fp16, int8/q4_0, q5_1 builds for the candidate open model (match SagePoint's baseline). Ensure kernel selection matches our production serving runtime.

3) Metrics and outputs (owner: Ben)
- Capture p50/p95/p99 latency, token amplification, hallucination flags per prompt, and a short human-eval sample for q variants. Put raw traces in the project Drive folder.

4) Commercial ops (owner: Rachel)
- Prepare a short cost delta estimate for running these probes at 30k qpm equivalent, and draft a Dedicated trial terms sketch if the results look good.

I'll start the infra reservation now and ping infra to confirm. Karthik — can you ack the model build plan by EOD?
